lazarus.title: Foundations Series: What The Hell-Part 5
lazarus.summary: The video reads the story as a parable built on a well-known ancient Egyptian fable, told to Pharisees who questioned why Jesus ate with sinners. Lazarus is Eleazar, Abraham's Gentile chief servant; the rich man in purple is the Jewish leadership. The shock is reversal: the outsider is in Abraham's bosom and the natural heirs are not. Jesus was not making doctrine about compartments of hell but showing that those thought to be out are in.
points: Jesus spoke Aramaic, not Greek; the video says tracing Lazarus back through the Greek to the Aramaic gives Eleazar, a name every Pharisee and Sadducee listening would recognize.
Eleazar was the chief servant Abraham named as his only heir before Isaac was born, a Gentile outside the covenant at that time, as Genesis 15:2-3 records.
The video calls the story an ancient Egyptian fable, as familiar to the hearers as Hansel and Gretel or the three little pigs are to us.
Jesus changed the fable: in the original the rich man has a name and the poor man has none, but Jesus names the poor man instead.
The hearers knew the wealthy man clothed in purple, who walked past the beggar every day, stood for them.
The video argues the listeners believed the dead slept with their fathers until the Messiah, so an afterlife lesson would not have enraged them; the insult was a Gentile in Abraham.
Like most of his parables, the story tells Jews that those they consider outsiders are now included, because the gospel is for all people.
lazarus.differs: The app's topic also reads Lazarus as Eleazar the Gentile steward, but frames the parable around stewardship and the love of money. The video adds an Egyptian fable source and a claim that the hearers tried to stone Jesus, which Luke 16 does not record.
